Private inputs and outputs live in ~/.graphonomous/v3-bench/. This repository is public.

The ruling (D-078), in short:

  • Graphonomous keeps v2's definition: a derived semantic graph over sources it does not own.

  • v2 gains the memory folder and the ruling register as sources. It keeps its deterministic, governed

relation mechanics, uses authored relations where a source states them, and abstains or queues for review otherwise.

  • BM25 stays outside the semantic core. The tool is scripts/memory-search.py in the root repository.

  • Not added:

  • a Graphonomous-owned memory store;

  • this spec's daemon (§4.8 A1), for recall;

  • its journal (§4.2);

  • model-mediated recall;

  • automatic Jev relation proposals.

  • A new major version needs a new invariant or execution model, not accumulated features.

  • One lane stays open, non-authoritative: candidate → model suggestion → human review. It measures

review load under a new predeclaration, and never tunes on V3-1 (b)'s test split.

Name trap — read before quoting this document. "v3" is already used twice in this repository: graphonomous.semantic.v3 is a profile id proposed by v2's R17 (the WRL vocabulary), and v2's stage roadmap numbers its stages G0–G5 (G3 = reduction). This document is about neither. Write Graphonomous v3 in full — never "v3" or "G3" alone — until [T1] settles the name.

0. In one paragraph

Graphonomous v1 (v0.4.3, Elixir, graphonomous/lib/) tried to be an agent's memory, and it deletes what it stores. Graphonomous v2 (graphonomous/v2/, Node ESM) is a certified evidence graph over pinned registries and has, deliberately, no write surface. Super, the MVP (R97), holds an unbuilt slot for "the memory each agent carries". Graphonomous v3 is the proposal to fill that slot: the memory substrate of an active locus, built on v2's projection and certificate machinery, fed by rulings, Super's receipts and proposed observations, and judged — never authored — by a calibrated typed decider (TypeSafe's Jev, or Ollaya, its free local counterpart). v2 is not modified: Graphonomous v3 adds a journal, profiles and adapters beside it. v1 becomes legacy (§6).

1. Why now

Each of those servers loaded the graph into memory once at start (warm_cache_from_db, store.ex), so a session never saw another session's writes, and each ran its own consolidator against the same file. "stored but retrieve returns 0" was not a crash: it was a forgetting curve tuned for benchmark churn, running as 29 independent copies of itself.

1.2 v2 is a different product — read from the tree

  • Its definition: *"the persistent semantic/evidence graph that makes what a system understands queryable,

falsifiable, provenance-linked, and reducible", and "a derived semantic projection over authoritative registries … not another authoritative registry"* (v2/README.md).

  • "No LLM output is evidence. Deterministic, content-addressed, replayable transforms only."

(v2/README.md:38).

  • D-071 (2026-09-03): "The next step is NOT a write surface."

  • Projections are rebuilt whole from a pinned snapshot; lib/project.mjs deletes the output directory

first. There is no append path.

  • The query surface is six structural functions (lib/query.mjs: node · neighbors · path · facts ·

explain · as_of); "Nothing here computes a fact the projection and its evaluation do not already hold." There is no relevance retrieval, no embedding, no MCP server.

  • Latest decision D-077; last commit 61adec2d (2026-09-08); full tree 182 pass / 0 fail / 1 skip.

So "move the MCP onto v2" is a category error as v2 stands: v1 answered what do we remember?, v2 answers what does the stack's evidence establish?

1.4 What actually carries continuity today — measured

The file memory at ~/.claude/projects/-home-travis-ProjectAmp2/memory/: 148 files, 34,886 lines, indexed by MEMORY.md. Not in git, not certified, not shared with Codex or Super — and it works. Any Graphonomous v3 has to beat it at its own job, or not be built (§8 F1).

1.5 The new thing — calibrated typed deciders — reported

Jev (TypeSafe AI, announced 2026-09-15) and Ollaya (Apache-2.0, released ≈ 2026-09-24, wire-compatible with Jev on POST /v1/systemone) answer typed questions about a state — noul (P(true)), choice (2–255 labels, a probability each), score (2–10 levels) — with calibrated probabilities and no text and no embeddings. They judge candidates; they cannot find them. Those are exactly the judgments v1 made with hard-coded constants — and a hard-coded constant (§1.1) is what emptied it. Details and sources: §10.

3. Principles

  • P1 — No model output is evidence (inherits v2/README.md:38). A decider's answer is a DECISION

record carrying its certificate: a ranking or a proposal, never a fact.

  • P2 — Floor, then gradient (box-and-box, feasible ▸ permitted ▸ best). Deterministic rules refuse

(§4.5); the decider only orders what the floor admitted. A decider never sits in permitted.

  • P3 — No second ledger. Facts about Super's world enter from Super's receipts. Graphonomous v3 reads

downstream and never writes into ampd's stores.

  • P4 — Nothing is forgotten by a constant. Retirement is a decision with a trigger and a record; it

archives. Erasure is a separate, explicit, audited command. (v1's lesson.)

  • P5 — One process owns the store. Every client is an adapter; no per-session engines. (v1's lesson.)

  • P6 — Rulings outrank observations. A REVISION_REGISTER.md row is authoritative; an observation

that contradicts a current ruling is admitted only as a flagged conflict.

  • P7 — Measured or cited. Every number has a command or a source; measured and reported stay apart.

  • P8 — Local and free first. Zero budget. Hosted Jev is a metered reference and fallback, not a

dependency.

  • P9 — Memory is per locus. AGENCY.md: "memory is a substrate; lineage is a relation." A Bot or

Worker recalls through its projection, not the world.

FamilyWhatAuthorityStatus

4.2 The journal — the one missing primitive

v2 can only rebuild. A memory has to append. Proposal: an append-only, framed, gapless-sequenced journal (the shape of Super's AuthorityLog: one record per admitted transition, jseq without holes). Projections become folds over journal ranges.

Law J-1: `fold(journal[0..n])` is byte-identical to `rebuild(snapshot at n)`. The full rebuild stays the verifier; the incremental fold is only the fast path. The journal is the only thing ever written; everything else is derived.

4.3 Record kinds — a new profile, never an edit to a frozen one

OBSERVATION · RULING · DECISION (one decider call: model id + weights digest, calibration version, question id@version, state hash, probabilities, confidence, latency, host) · RETIREMENT (what was archived, its trigger, and the rule or DECISION that caused it). Relations: SUPERSEDES (ruling→ruling, observation→observation), CONTRADICTS (a flag, never a verdict), CITES, CORROBORATED_BY (observation → receipt | evidence | ruling). Whether this is a graphonomous.semantic.vN profile or a separate graphonomous.memory.v0 family is [T6].

4.4 Recall — finding candidates

A decider cannot find anything; it only judges what it is shown. Recall is lexical (full-text over OBSERVATION and RULING text), plus structural (v2's neighbors / path), plus embeddings if [T7] says so. v1's fallback hash embedder is not semantic recall and is not carried over. Recall returns at most 255 candidates, the decider's choice bound.

4.5 Floor — deterministic refusals the decider cannot weaken

  • F-1 An OBSERVATION without an author locus and a session is refused.

  • F-2 Secret-shaped text (API keys, passwords, tokens) is refused at intake. Local files on this

machine are known to hold plaintext credentials, and no import may carry them. (A file path stood here until 2026-09-28. It was removed because this repository is public.)

  • F-3 A RULING is superseded only by a later RULING, never by an observation.

  • F-4 An observation that contradicts a current ruling is admitted flagged CONTRADICTS, never as

current.

  • F-5 Nothing is deleted by the engine. Retirement archives; erasure is its own audited command.

  • F-6 A DECISION with an incomplete certificate is refused: absent ⇒ 0̲, fail closed (AGENCY.md,

certificate).

  • F-7 Proposals are metered per locus. Alphapiler measured it (Piles of Dust, PASS 9): when refusals

cost nothing, a blind picker asking often beats an informed one asking rarely.

4.6 Judge — the question catalogue

IdTypeQuestionAnswer goes toReplaces in v1
Q-KEEPnoulIs this a durable fact worth carrying beyond this session?review order at intakestore-everything
Q-ASSERTnoulIs it stated as settled (vs a plan, guess, question)?a tag—
Q-SAMEscore ×3different / review / same, for a candidate pairmerge proposalconsolidator_merge_similarity 0.95
Q-CONTRAnoulDo these two contradict?CONTRADICTS candidate— (v2 reduced its two conflict rules to zero, D-074, restated in D-076)
Q-SUPERSEDEchoicea supersedes b / b supersedes a / both stand / reviewSUPERSEDES proposal—
Q-RANKchoicewhich of these ≤255 candidates answers the query?recall ordersimilarity score
Q-ENOUGHnoulIs this enough to act?act / learn / escalate hint — second opinion to κ routing, never an overridecoverage heuristic
Q-RETIREchoicekeep / archive / review — asked only on a trigger (superseded, contradicted, source moved), never on a timerRETIREMENT proposaldecay 0.02 / prune 0.1

Probabilities are stored, not thresholded at write time; the threshold that acts is part of the question's version. The middle band goes to a review queue (Travis, or a stronger model), never to an automatic merge. Calibration is refitted per question type on our own labels: reported, calibration drifts in a different direction per question type out of distribution (§10).

4.7 Where the decider runs — [T2]

  • Option A — inside the Graphonomous v3 daemon (plain HTTP to a local Ollaya). Latency is reported at

89–520 ms on an RTX 4090. That answers the first reason behind the standing rule "MCP servers make no LLM calls" (calls of 60–130 s timed out). Every call is a DECISION record, which answers the second (visibility). It still contradicts the rule as worded.

  • Option B — agent-asked. The daemon returns typed questions; the agent asks the decider and submits the

answers. The rule stays intact, but the daemon cannot establish that an answer came from the named model: a submitted certificate is only a claim.

  • Option C — a Super capability. Inside Super the decider is a capability pack, and each call is an

effect through Gateway whose receipt is the certificate. The most Super-native option; waits on Super.

Recommendation: C inside Super; A outside it if [T2] permits; B only as the interim.

4.8 Access

  • A1 — one MCP daemon for Claude Code and Codex sessions outside Super. A systemd user unit, like

super-desktop, serving HTTP on 127.0.0.1. The plugin points at its URL: no stdio spawn per session (P5). Tools: recall, explain, status, then propose; read-only first. Reported: the MCP spec of 2026-07-28 made the protocol core stateless (no session id), so a continuation is an explicit handle returned by a tool.

  • A2 — a `memory` capability pack inside Super. Reads through the agent and bot projections

(ampd/lib/ampd/projection.ex); proposals go through Gateway.perform and come back as receipts. Super's own Claude and Codex hosts stay --strict-mcp-config.

  • A3 — CLI. recall / explain over the memory profiles, beside v2's bin/g0.mjs query.

4.9 Resource budget on this machine — measured

30 GB RAM under chronic pressure (the desktop app has been OOM-killed at 14–23 GB resident); an RTX 4060 Laptop GPU with 8,188 MiB; glibc 2.44 (Ollaya reportedly needs ≥ 2.38). v2 reads whole JSONL files into memory (lib/evaluation.mjs), and its projections/ hold 296 MB on disk. Before any promise: measure the daemon's idle and peak RSS, and each candidate decider model's resident size. Candidates: decider:2b or winnow:e4b; laya only for short pairs (reported 421M, 512-token context). [T3]

8. Falsifiers — what stops or shrinks Graphonomous v3

  • F1 If V3-1(a) recall does not beat index + grep on real questions, J1 is not worth building: keep the

file memory and stop at v2. Fired 2026-09-28, in the "not shown" sense (§7 V3-1 (a)).

  • On this evidence, a daemon, journal and decider are not justified for recall.

  • The proportionate step is a ranked search (BM25) over the memory folder. It beat grep by +0.049 with a

95 % CI of [+0.004, +0.092], just under the predeclared 0.05 margin.

  • Re-test if the memory grows well past 147 notes, or if questions become sentences rather than keyword

bags.

  • F2 If no decider beats its deterministic baseline on our labels, drop the judge. Graphonomous v3 keeps

the floor and recall. For recall (Q-RANK), the first reading is negative (−0.020 against its own BM25 candidates). For relation judgment, it fired 2026-09-28 (§7 V3-1 (b)).

  • Governed Jev beat both fixed rules on cost, but it did not beat refusing to mutate. It asserted false

supersessions with high confidence.

  • Under the predeclared rule, v2's relation proposals stay deterministic or manual.

  • Untested: a decider that only queues relations for human review (94 % of governed Jev's answers

were right); Ollaya; any other prompt or model.

  • F3 If law J-1 fails on any range, the journal design is wrong, and rebuild stays the only path.

  • F4 If a DECISION cannot be replayed to the same answer on the same model digest (reported: fp16

can flip near-ties), decisions are recorded as non-replayable and may not gate anything.

  • F5 If Super's receipt shape changes during stage 0, V3-6 waits. Nothing earlier depends on it.

9. Open rulings [TRAVIS]

Closed 2026-09-28. The disposition of every T# is in §C at the top.

  • T1 — Name. "Graphonomous v3", or a distinct name that cannot collide with semantic.v3 or G3.

Evidence since, 2026-09-28: both V3-1 benches came back negative for the new machinery.

  • (a): recall is served by BM25 over the folder.

  • (b): a typed decider may not propose relations.

  • What survives is v2 plus two source families (the memory folder and the ruling register) and an

external BM25 tool, with relation proposals left deterministic or manual.

  • That is an argument that there is no v3, only v2 growing. Not a ruling: whether v3 exists is

Travis's call.

  • T2 — Where the decider runs (§4.7), and whether "MCP servers make no LLM calls" covers a local,

recorded, sub-second decider.

  • T3 — Installing Ollaya. The installer is curl -fsSL https://ollaya.dev/install.sh | sh from a

project days old (reported: v0.3.1 → v0.7.3 between 2026-09-24 and 2026-09-27), or a pinned build from source. Which model, given 8 GB of VRAM.

  • T4 — Gates. The quality and calibration thresholds a question must meet to enter the catalogue.

  • T5 — Confidentiality. Does carried memory hold personal or secret content? This is the same question

as studbook §10.2 (content addressing versus access control), and F-2 is only the floor of it.

  • T6 — Profile family. graphonomous.semantic.vN, or a separate graphonomous.memory.v0.

  • T7 — Embeddings. Which local model, or none (lexical plus structural recall only).

  • T8 — The file memory's role. A source Graphonomous v3 imports, or the primary store with Graphonomous

v3 as a certified index over it. Evidence since, 2026-09-28: about 11× as many sessions used the folder as used v1 (310 vs 28), and plain search over it already puts a first-read note at rank 1 for 78–83 % of the real questions (grep 78 %, BM25 83 %). Both favour "primary store". Not a ruling.

10. Research record — reported, fetched 2026-09-27 by a web research pass, not reproduced here

Ollaya — github.com/ollaya-dev/ollaya, ollaya.dev, API.

  • Rust, Apache-2.0, "not affiliated with Ollama or TypeSafe". The creator is named elsewhere as Mert Cobanov.

  • Default address 127.0.0.1:11435. POST /v1/systemone and /v1/decisions, an Ollama-style /api/tags,

and a native /api/decide.

  • Limits: 1–256 questions per request and 65,536 state tokens, with STATE_TRUNCATED rather than a silent

drop.

  • Models run on ONNX Runtime (CPU / CUDA / MLX), and GGUF models on llama.cpp (since v0.7.0).

  • A decoder model answers by reading the final-layer scores for the option letters at Answer: ( and

softmaxing over the valid letters: one pass, no generation. Calibration is per-model temperature scaling.

  • ollaya mcp shipped in v0.4.0. It has no embeddings and no fine-tuning inside Ollaya; the upstream

decider model documents a LoRA recipe.

  • Author-measured on an RTX 4090 against hosted Jev at 0.738 (which includes network time): winnow:e4b

0.722 @ 89 ms, decider:4b 0.680 @ 520 ms, laya 0.361 @ ≈ 10 ms. JevBench v1.4.2.2 (benchmarkheaven.com/jev-models): decider-4b v2 64.1, Jev 1.13.0 63.3.

Jev — TypeSafe blog, OpenRouter guide.

  • Proprietary, "System One": a non-autoregressive single pass. $0.042 per million input tokens; output is

free. typesafe/jev-1.13.

  • There is no official calibration figure. An out-of-distribution study

(scienthoon/jev-ood-calibration) measured ECE 0.107, erring in a different direction per question type.

  • Already used live in this tree by alphapiler (~/Projects/Travelmonstr/alphapiler/src/jev.js).

Deciders in memory systems

  • lyonwj.com, knowledge-graph extraction:

  • a two-question noul assertion gate lifted precision 0.279 → 0.404 with no lost true edges;

  • a 3-level score for entity resolution lifted B³ F1 0.946 → 1.000;

  • a noul contradiction check separated planted contradictions where cosine similarity could not;

  • and "a System One model can't find an edge."

  • arXiv 2609.23986 (Jev-Mem): Jev as the memory controller for typing,

dedup/contradiction and retrieval routing; LoCoMo 0.777 against 0.700 for the best baseline.

  • Memworthy: gated memory with eight actions and a replayable

JSONL ledger.

  • No integration was found in Graphiti/Zep, Letta, cognee, LangMem or the official MCP memory servers.

MCP — 2026-07-28 release: a stateless core (no handshake, no Mcp-Session-Id), Tasks as an extension, and Roots / Sampling / Logging deprecated.

Could not verify: Ollaya's first-release date; the exact tool names ollaya mcp exposes; whether Ollaya can refit temperatures from user labels; any Jev architecture detail; and latency on this machine's GPU. The sources also disagree on Jev's calibration error (0.027 vs 0.246) and its accuracy (0.727 vs 0.738).
